protocol.summary: Quiet-machine window. Each process is one sample. K = 9 = 3 passes x 3 rounds (pass 0 reversed, pass 1 forward, pass 2 reversed); the arms of a comparison run adjacent. A sample counts only if the machine was at most 5 % busy before and after it, other processes used at most 2 % during it, and no build ran; unclean samples are re-run at the end of the pass (up to 4 waves). A pass in which an arm has fewer than 3 clean samples gates nothing. CLAIMED = the IQR test and the SE test both pass in every pass and pooled, with one sign; STRONG = the min-max test passes too; otherwise NOT RESOLVED with the demonstrated resolution. A claim reads one launch only.
protocol.claim_rule: per cell: median, i = IQR/median, s = 1.2533*SD/sqrt(K)/median, r = (max-min)/median; a test flags when |ours/other - 1| > 2*sqrt(x_ours^2 + x_other^2); CLAIMED iff i and s flag in every pass and pooled with one sign; STRONG iff r flags too
protocol.print_rule: r = ours cell / other cell; a CLAIMED comparison prints "X.XX x faster" (r < 1) or "X.XX x slower" (r > 1) with X.XX = max(r, 1/r) rounded to 2 decimals; the subject is always boyko; a NOT RESOLVED comparison prints only "no measurable difference at this resolution (X %)", X rounded up to one decimal
protocol.ratio_field: ratio.factor is the print-rule factor (never below 1) and ratio.word its sign word; ratio is null for NOT_RESOLVED and DESCRIPTIVE entries
protocol.not_resolved_cells: NOT_RESOLVED entries carry no values (ours and other.value are null), so no ratio can be read from them
protocol.one_launch: every printed entry comes from launch 2 (run tag 195316, 2026-10-09 19:53-23:26 UTC+03:00); nothing from launch 1 is printed
protocol.validity: every process: executable sha256 equal to its pin; every physics process: final pose byte-equal to its pinned fixture (Jolt: its state hash); 0 mismatches

launches.why: the Claude desktop app was active; most samples were unclean; Windows hung at about 16:11

notes: Slowdown regime: a machine-wide slowdown co-occurs with the Claude desktop app being active and passes the CPU-load guard. In launch 1 clean samples ran 8.9 % (boyko), 6.5 % (Jolt) and 32-39 % (Rapier) slower than in launch 2, while in launch 1's quiet minutes (16:05-16:12) boyko and Jolt matched launch 2 within 1 %. The most likely cause is the laptop's shared CPU/GPU power budget. In launch 2 the app was idle until about 22:50; the second micro-benchmark set's third process, the GPU block and the sleeping block ran after that.

Drift: the same boyko and Jolt executables took 2.5-12.0 % (boyko) and 8.5-21.3 % (Jolt) less time per step on the dynamic scenes in this window than in an earlier window on the same machine (early 2026-10-09). The factors are a dated snapshot of one machine state.

Diagnostics profile: no boyko binary was built with BOYKO_PROFILE set, so the diagnostics profile is the default dev (profiling zones compiled in); the physics runner reports profile_name dev and zones_compiled true in every process. "Shipped configuration" in the labels means the Cargo codegen (fat LTO, x86-64-v3). The setting adds work on boyko's side only.

Rapier labels: an earlier window (9b, 2026-10-05) screened a frozen set of 70 Rapier configurations on the resting pile; "9b's J-T rank-1 row" is the fastest configuration that keeps the pile standing at that worker count. It was not re-screened on these scenes, so it is never called "Rapier's fastest on this scene". s1p9q2 is the only Rapier configuration that holds the 88-run fidelity ensemble.

headlines.text: boyko physics is 1.08 x to 1.18 x faster than Jolt 5.6 in 13 of 15 comparisons on three dynamic scenes (kick, shoot, slide) at 1-16 worker threads, sleeping off in both engines (all claimed, 8 claimed STRONG); slide at W8 and W16 shows no measurable difference at this resolution (5.6 % and 5.2 %).
boyko physics is 1.39 x to 2.31 x slower than Rapier 0.36 in all 30 comparisons on the same scenes (all claimed, 27 claimed STRONG).

vs bevy_ecs 0.18.1, both engines built in the shipped configuration (fat LTO, x86-64-v3), Windows system heap: boyko_ecs is 2.86 x faster on 50 empty systems, 2.70 x faster growing one archetype to 1 M entities (Bevy not pre-reserved) and 1.95 x faster growing 16 archetypes to 960k entities (claimed STRONG); it is 1.67 x slower on direct 10k-row query iteration (claimed STRONG), 1.17 x slower on spawn_batch of 10k (claimed), and 5.89 x slower on a 10k-row query through a system the harness rebuilds every iteration (claimed STRONG; a harness artifact).
